params.body:
Links between trends: which ones reinforce each other, and which pull against each other.

**Why:** a strategist combines trends. Until now nothing said which ones belong together. The Standard only knows "related" and "opposing" between concepts, not between trends.

**How a link comes about:** it is judged, not counted.
- The graph proposes neighbours by shared concepts.
- A model judges each pair from both sides: `reinforces`, `pulls` or none.
- Only a verdict both sides agree on is written.
- On 2026-09-28: 105 pairs proposed, 49 kept (43 reinforces, 6 pulls), reviewed on a page.
- The graph's own "opposing" edges were not usable. 3,353 automatically named tensions tied unrelated trends together (734 pairs).

**Changes**
- **`core/trend-links.mjs`:**
  - `trend_links` (a < b, kind, why) and `setLink`.
  - `linksOf(id, live)` returns `[{id, kind, why}]` from either side, `pulls` first, only to trends in `live`.
  - A folded trend hands its links to the trend that took it over; a link that would point at itself is dropped.
- **`listShowcaseInsights`:** every trend carries `links`, only to trends that are themselves shown, so every link opens a page.
- **`bin/assign-links.mjs --from <list> [--apply]`:** writes a reviewed list `[{a, b, kind, why}]`. It is dry by default, and only live trends and known kinds are written.

**After merge:** write the 49 reviewed links. The site gets its PR to show them and to pass them through the MCP.

Checks: new `test/trend-links.test.mjs` (both sides, pulls first, only live, folding, refusals); 959 tests, 0 failures.
params.title: Trends that belong together, and trends that pull against each other
